title: Penal Code
summary: Principal criminal statute defining offences, defences, and punishments in Kenya.
full_text:
The Penal Code (Cap. 63) establishes criminal offences and penalties in Kenya.

Part I — Preliminary: This Act may be cited as the Penal Code.

Part II — General Principles: A person is not criminally responsible for an act or omission if at the time of doing the act the person was in such a state of mental disease or natural mental infirmity as to deprive the person of capacity to understand what the person is doing.

Part III — Offences against public order: Treason, sedition, unlawful assemblies and riots.

Part IV — Offences against the administration of lawful authority: Escape from lawful custody, resisting officers, perjury.

Part V — Offences against person: Murder, manslaughter, assault, causing grievous harm, defilement, rape, kidnapping.

Murder (s. 203): Any person who of malice aforethought causes death of another person by an unlawful act or omission is guilty of murder.

Manslaughter (s. 202): Any person who by an unlawful act or omission causes the death of another person is guilty of the felony termed manslaughter.

Theft (s. 275): Any person who steals anything capable of being stolen is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years unless the punishment is elsewhere prescribed.

Robbery with violence (s. 296(2)): If the offender is armed with a dangerous or offensive weapon, or is in company with one or more other person or persons, or if, at or immediately before or immediately after the time of the robbery, the offender wounds, beats, strikes, or uses any other personal violence to any person, the offender is liable to suffer death.

sections.heading: Murder
sections.text: Any person who of malice aforethought causes death of another person by an unlawful act or omission is guilty of murder.

sections.heading: Punishment of murder
sections.text: Any person who is convicted of murder shall be sentenced to death, subject to Article 26 of the Constitution and judicial interpretation regarding mandatory death sentences.

sections.heading: Stealing
sections.text: Any person who steals anything capable of being stolen is guilty of a felony and is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to imprisonment for three years.

sections.heading: Robbery with violence
sections.text: Every person who commits the felony of robbery is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years. If the offender is armed with a dangerous or offensive weapon, or is in company with one or more other person, or wounds, beats or uses personal violence, the offender is liable to suffer death.

title: Criminal Procedure Code
summary: Governs procedure in criminal trials, arrest, bail, charge sheets, and appeals in criminal matters.
full_text:
The Criminal Procedure Code regulates how criminal proceedings are conducted in Kenya.

Arrest: A police officer may arrest without warrant any person reasonably suspected of having committed an offence.

Bail: Subject to Article 49, an accused person is entitled to be released on bail pending trial unless there are compelling reasons.

Preliminary inquiry / committal: In the High Court, committal proceedings apply to offences triable by the High Court.

Trial: The court shall take evidence of the prosecution first. The accused is entitled to cross-examine witnesses. After the prosecution case, the court may rule there is no case to answer under section 210, or put the accused on defence.

Section 210 — No case to answer: If at the close of the evidence for the prosecution, the court considers that there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence, the court shall dismiss the charge and acquit the accused.

Section 347 — Appeals from subordinate courts: An appeal lies to the High Court from a conviction or sentence of a subordinate court.

sections.heading: Rights of arrested person (constitutional overlay)
sections.text: An accused person must be brought before a court within 24 hours and is entitled to bail on reasonable conditions.

sections.heading: No case to answer
sections.text: If at the close of the case for the prosecution the court considers that there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence, the court shall dismiss the charge and acquit the accused.

sections.heading: Appeals from subordinate courts
sections.text: An appeal shall lie to the High Court from a conviction or sentence of a subordinate court.

title: Evidence Act
summary: Rules on admissibility, relevance, burden and standard of proof, and witness competence in Kenyan courts.
full_text:
The Evidence Act (Cap. 80) governs what evidence may be received and how it is assessed.

Relevance: Facts not in issue but so connected with a fact in issue as to form part of the same transaction are relevant.

Hearsay: Generally inadmissible subject to statutory exceptions and constitutional fair-trial guarantees.

Confessions: A confession made by an accused person is inadmissible if obtained by oppression, violence, threat or promise.

Burden of proof: The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the court to believe in its existence.

Standard of proof: In civil cases the standard is balance of probabilities; in criminal cases it is beyond reasonable doubt.

Electronic evidence: Electronic records may be admissible if authenticity can be established.

Character evidence: In criminal proceedings, evidence of bad character is generally inadmissible to prove conduct, subject to exceptions.

sections.heading: Relevant facts
sections.text: Facts which, either by themselves or when taken with other facts, make the existence of the fact in issue probable or improbable are relevant.

sections.heading: Confessions
sections.text: A confession made by an accused person is inadmissible if it appears to the court to have been caused by any violent, oppressive, inhuman or degrading conduct or threat.

sections.heading: Burden of proof
sections.text: Whoever desires any court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts must prove that those facts exist.

title: Law of Contract Act
summary: Formation, performance, breach, and remedies for contracts in Kenya.
full_text:
The Law of Contract Act codifies general principles of contract law in Kenya.

Offer and acceptance: A contract arises when an offer is accepted without qualification.

Consideration: An agreement made without consideration is void unless made by deed or under statutory exception.

Capacity: Minors and persons of unsound mind have limited contractual capacity.

Written contracts: Certain contracts must be evidenced in writing (e.g., guarantees, disposition of interests in land under Article 40 and Land Registration Act).

Breach and damages: The injured party is entitled to damages reasonably arising from the breach, subject to remoteness rules.

Specific performance: Available as an equitable remedy where damages are inadequate.

sections.heading: Agreements made without consideration void
sections.text: An agreement made without consideration is void, unless it is expressed in writing and registered or is a promise to compensate for something done or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation.

sections.heading: Contract in restraint of trade
sections.text: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind is to that extent void.

title: Employment Act
summary: Primary statute on employment relationships, contracts, termination, leave, and workplace rights.
full_text:
The Employment Act 2007 is the principal statute governing employment in Kenya.

Written contracts: An employer shall give an employee a written statement of particulars of employment.

Probation: Probationary employment shall not exceed six months but may be extended once for a further six months with consent.

Equal pay: An employer shall pay employees equal remuneration for work of equal value.

Termination: Employment may be terminated fairly for incapacity, misconduct, redundancy, or other valid reason after a fair procedure.

Unfair termination: Termination is unfair if the employer fails to prove a valid reason or fails to follow fair procedure (notice, hearing).

Remedies: Compensation up to 12 months' gross wages for unfair termination; reinstatement or re-engagement may be ordered by the Employment and Labour Relations Court.

Leave: Annual leave of at least 21 working days with full pay after twelve consecutive months of service. Sick leave and maternity/paternity leave as prescribed.

sections.heading: Employment contract
sections.text: A contract of service for a period exceeding three months shall be in writing and shall state the names of the parties, date of commencement, form and duration of the contract, place of work, job description, remuneration and method of calculation, and leave entitlement.

sections.heading: Termination notice
sections.text: Either party may terminate a contract of service by giving notice. Notice periods depend on the interval of payment of wages.

sections.heading: Notification and hearing before termination
sections.text: An employer shall, before terminating the employment of an employee, notify the employee of the reasons and give the employee an opportunity to make representations.

sections.heading: Complaint of unfair termination
sections.text: An employee may present a complaint alleging unfair termination to the labour officer or the Employment and Labour Relations Court.

title: Land Act
summary: Governs land tenure, rights, compulsory acquisition, leases, and public land management.
full_text:
The Land Act 2012 gives effect to Article 63–64 of the Constitution on land tenure.

Categories of land: Public, community, and private land.

All land in Kenya belongs to the people of Kenya collectively as a nation, as communities and as individuals.

Private land: Land registered under freehold or leasehold tenure.

Community land: Land vested in communities identified on the basis of ethnicity, culture or similar interest.

Public land: Land held by the national government in trust for the people of Kenya.

Compulsory acquisition: The National Land Commission may recommend compulsory acquisition for a public purpose or in the public interest, subject to fair compensation and public participation.

Leases: Leasehold interests may be granted for a term not exceeding 99 years for private land.

sections.heading: Categories of land
sections.text: Land in Kenya shall be classified as public, community or private land.

sections.heading: Compulsory acquisition
sections.text: The President shall acquire land on behalf of the national government for a public purpose or in the public interest upon recommendation of the National Land Commission, following inquiry and payment of compensation.

title: Environmental Management and Co-ordination Act
summary: Framework for environmental protection, EIA, NEMA powers, and environmental offences.
full_text:
EMCA is Kenya's principal environmental statute.

Every person has a duty to safeguard and enhance the environment.

Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is mandatory for projects likely to have significant environmental effects.

NEMA may issue restoration orders, improvement notices, and prohibition notices.

The National Environment Tribunal hears appeals from NEMA decisions.

Environmental offences include pollution of water, air, and soil; illegal dumping; and failure to conduct EIA.

sections.heading: Duty to safeguard environment
sections.text: Every person in Kenya has a duty to safeguard and enhance the environment.

sections.heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
sections.text: A project proponent shall not implement a project that is likely to have significant environmental effects unless an EIA study has been conducted and a licence issued by NEMA.

title: Political Parties Act
summary: Registration, funding, and regulation of political parties in Kenya.
full_text: The Political Parties Act establishes the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties and regulates party registration, symbols, funding, and codes of conduct. Political parties must have a national character and promote the values in Articles 10 and 91 of the Constitution.

title: Co-operative Societies Act
summary: Registration and regulation of co-operative societies in Kenya.
full_text: The Co-operative Societies Act provides for the establishment, registration, supervision, and dissolution of co-operative societies. Societies are managed by elected committees subject to the Commissioner for Co-operative Development. Disputes may be referred to the Co-operative Tribunal.

title: Insolvency Act
summary: Corporate and personal insolvency, liquidation, administration, and bankruptcy.
full_text: The Insolvency Act modernises Kenya's insolvency law. It provides for liquidation of companies, voluntary administration, schemes of arrangement, and personal bankruptcy. The official receiver and courts oversee processes. Secured creditors' rights and preferential debts are regulated.

title: Companies Act
summary: Incorporation, governance, directors' duties, and winding up of companies.
full_text: The Companies Act 2015 governs company formation and operation in Kenya, including private and public companies, directors' duties, members' rights, share capital, and corporate rescue. Companies are registered with the Business Registration Service.

title: Matrimonial Property Act
summary: Ownership and division of matrimonial property upon divorce or separation.
full_text: The Matrimonial Property Act recognises that spouses have equal proprietary rights. Matrimonial property includes the matrimonial home, household goods, and other property acquired during marriage. Contribution may be monetary or non-monetary including domestic work and farm labour.

title: Law of Succession Act
summary: Wills, intestate succession, grants of representation, and administration of estates.
full_text:
The Law of Succession Act governs inheritance in Kenya.

A person may dispose of free property by will.

Where a person dies intestate, the estate devolves according to statutory rules, with the surviving spouse and children having priority claims.

Grants of probate or letters of administration are issued by the High Court or Resident Magistrates' courts with jurisdiction.

Dependants may apply for reasonable provision from an estate under section 26.

sections.heading: Provision for dependants
sections.text: Where a deceased person has left a will that fails to make reasonable provision for a dependant, the court may order reasonable provision out of the net estate.

sections.heading: Intestate succession — surviving spouse and children
sections.text: Where an intestate has left one surviving spouse and a child or children, the surviving spouse shall be entitled to personal and household effects absolutely and to a life interest in the whole residue of the net intestate estate.

title: Public Benefit Organizations Act
summary: Registration and regulation of public benefit organizations (NGOs, CBOs).
full_text: The Public Benefit Organizations Act provides for registration, governance, and accountability of organisations that exist for public benefit. The Regulatory Authority maintains the register and may cancel registrations for non-compliance.

title: Data Protection Act
summary: Protection of personal data, data subject rights, and regulation of data controllers.
full_text: The Data Protection Act implements Article 31(c) and (d) of the Constitution. It establishes the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner. Processing of personal data requires lawful basis. Data subjects have rights of access, rectification, erasure, and objection. Cross-border transfers are regulated.

title: Access to Information Act
summary: Gives effect to Article 35 on access to information held by public entities.
full_text: Every citizen has the right of access to information held by the State and by another person and required for the exercise or protection of any right. Public entities must publish and publicise important information. Requests may be refused on limited grounds including privacy, security, and commercial confidence.

title: Income Tax Act
summary: Principal statute imposing tax on income of persons resident and non-resident in Kenya.
full_text:
The Income Tax Act (Cap. 470) charges tax on income of every person for each year of income.

Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxed on income sourced in Kenya.

Charge of tax: There shall be charged for each year of income tax upon income of every person for each year of income.

Deductions: Outgoings and expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in the production of income are deductible subject to statutory limits.

Withholding tax: Specific payments to non-residents and specified resident persons attract withholding tax at prescribed rates.

Capital allowances: Wear and tear and industrial building deductions are available for qualifying assets.

Transfer pricing: Transactions with associated enterprises must meet the arm's length principle.

sections.heading: Charge of tax
sections.text: There shall be charged for each year of income tax upon the income of every person for each year of income.

sections.heading: Deductions
sections.text: For the purpose of ascertaining the gains or profits, there shall be deducted all outgoings and expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in the production of that income.

sections.heading: Withholding tax
sections.text: A resident person making a payment to a non-resident person shall deduct tax at the prescribed rate and remit to the Commissioner.

title: Value Added Tax Act
summary: Imposes VAT on taxable supplies of goods and services in Kenya.
full_text:
The VAT Act 2013 provides for the imposition of value added tax on taxable supplies, imports, and related matters.

Standard rate of VAT applies to taxable supplies unless exempt or zero-rated.

A registered person making taxable supplies must account for output tax and may claim input tax subject to documentary requirements.

The Cabinet Secretary may by order amend the schedules of exempt and zero-rated goods with parliamentary approval.

Offences include failure to register, false returns, and failure to issue tax invoices.

sections.heading: VAT on taxable supplies
sections.text: VAT shall be charged on any taxable supply of goods or services made in Kenya by a registered person in the course of business.

sections.heading: Registration
sections.text: A person who makes taxable supplies exceeding the registration threshold shall apply for registration.

title: Children Act
summary: Consolidates and reformulates law relating to children in Kenya, including care, protection and justice.
full_text:
The Children Act 2022 gives effect to Article 53 of the Constitution and the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

Best interests of the child shall be the primary consideration in all actions concerning children.

The Act covers parental responsibility, foster care, adoption, child justice, and protection from abuse, exploitation and harmful practices.

Detention of children shall be a measure of last resort and for the shortest appropriate period.

sections.heading: Best interests of the child
sections.text: In all actions concerning children, the best interests of the child shall be the primary consideration.

sections.heading: Right to education
sections.text: Every child has the right to free and compulsory basic education.

title: Fair Administrative Action Act
summary: Gives effect to Article 47 on fair administrative action and procedural fairness.
full_text:
The Fair Administrative Action Act operationalises Article 47 of the Constitution.

Every person has the right to administrative action that is expeditious, efficient, lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair.

Where a right is adversely affected, the person is entitled to written reasons for the decision.

Administrative bodies must give prior notice, opportunity to make representations, and notice of appeal or review rights.

The High Court may review administrative action on grounds of illegality, irrationality, procedural impropriety, and breach of legitimate expectation.

sections.heading: Administrative action to be expeditious, efficient, lawful
sections.text: Every person has the right to administrative action which is expeditious, efficient, lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair.

sections.heading: Prior notice
sections.text: A person likely to be adversely affected by an administrative decision is entitled to prior notice of the proposed decision and reasons for it.

sections.heading: Written reasons
sections.text: Where an administrative action is likely to adversely affect rights, the administrator shall give written reasons for the action.

title: Competition Act
summary: Promotes and protects competition in Kenyan markets; regulates mergers and consumer protection.
full_text:
The Competition Act prohibits anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominant position; provides for merger control; and protects consumers against unfair practices.

The Competition Authority of Kenya investigates and adjudicates competition offences.

Exclusionary abuses include predatory pricing, refusal to deal, and tied selling where the effect is to substantially prevent or lessen competition.

Mergers require prior notification and approval where thresholds are met.

sections.heading: Restrictive trade practices
sections.text: An agreement between undertakings is prohibited if its object or effect is the prevention, restriction or distortion of competition.

sections.heading: Abuse of dominant position
sections.text: An undertaking which holds a dominant position in a market is prohibited from abusing that position.

title: Insurance Act
summary: Regulates insurance business, licensing of insurers and intermediaries in Kenya.
full_text: The Insurance Act regulates the carrying on of insurance business in Kenya. Insurers must be licensed by the Insurance Regulatory Authority. The Act covers long-term and general insurance business, professional indemnity, and policyholder protection.

title: Banking Act
summary: Licensing and regulation of financial institutions by the Central Bank of Kenya.
full_text: The Banking Act requires institutions taking deposits to be licensed by the Central Bank. It covers capital requirements, liquidity, lending limits, confidentiality of customer information, and resolution of troubled institutions.

sections.heading: Restriction on disclosure of customer information
sections.text: No person shall disclose customer account information except as required by law or with customer consent.

title: Married Women Property Act
summary: Historical statute on married women's property, read with Matrimonial Property Act and Constitution.
full_text: Read with the Constitution (Articles 27, 40, 45) and Matrimonial Property Act 2013, this Act historically enabled married women to hold property in their own name. Modern disputes turn on contribution (monetary and non-monetary) to acquisition of matrimonial property.

title: Land Registration Act
summary: Governs registration of interests in land, titles, caveats and land registries.
full_text: The Land Registration Act 2012 provides for the registration of title to land and interests in land. Registration confers indefeasibility subject to fraud, overriding interests and statutory exceptions. The Act covers transfers, leases, charges, caveats and rectification of the register.

sections.heading: Registration as conclusive evidence of proprietorship
sections.text: The certificate of title issued upon registration shall be taken by all courts as prima facie evidence that the person named is the proprietor.

title: National Land Commission Act
summary: Establishes the National Land Commission and its functions under Article 67.
full_text: The National Land Commission Act gives effect to Article 67. The Commission manages public land on behalf of the national and county governments; recommends a national land policy; investigates and resolves historical land injustices; and recommends a fair process for compulsory acquisition.

title: County Governments Act
summary: Provides for county government functions, intergovernmental relations and county assemblies.
full_text: The County Governments Act elaborates on Chapter Eleven of the Constitution. It covers county executive and assembly functions, public participation, county planning, and intergovernmental dispute resolution.

title: Public Participation and Access to Information
summary: Constitutional baseline for public participation in legislative and policy processes.
full_text: Kenyan courts have developed a substantial jurisprudence requiring meaningful public participation before enactment of legislation and county laws. Requirements include timely notice, accessible information, opportunity to make submissions, and consideration of views received. Failure to involve the public may invalidate the enactment.
